answer_text:
Here are **essential tips to avoid fake job scams**, especially important as reported job-related scams have jumped more than 1,000% recently, according to research by Newsweek and McAfee.

---

## 🔍 1. Research the Company Thoroughly
Scammers often create fake job listings that appear legitimate. Always check the official employer website to see if the job is listed there. If it's not, it might be a scam. You can also look up the employer on Google and LinkedIn to make sure it's real and has actual employees.

---

## 💸 2. Never Pay for a Job
Don't pay for the promise of a job. Honest employers, including the federal government, will never ask you to pay to get a job. Anyone who does is a scammer.

---

## 📧 3. Watch Out for Suspicious Emails
Scammers frequently fake emails with free web-based email accounts such as Gmail or Yahoo, and use slightly modified versions of the official employer's domain name. Be very suspicious of offers from Gmail, Yahoo, or similar personal email domains, as legitimate recruiters typically use corporate email accounts.

---

## 🚩 4. Be Wary of "Too Good to Be True" Offers
If a job offer seems too good to be true — enormous salary or fantastic perks with minimal effort required — it probably is. Be cautious of unrealistic promises, as this is a common tactic used by scammers to lure people in.

---

## ⏱️ 5. Don't Be Rushed
Take your time. Fraudulent job employers will pressure you to act quickly by paying or sharing personal information with them. A real employer would not pressure you to make a quick decision.

---

## 🔒 6. Protect Your Personal Information
Never provide sensitive personal information (your Social Security number or bank details) early in the hiring process. Legitimate employers usually wait to ask for this information until later in the hiring process — typically on the first day of work.

---

## ✅ 7. Verify the Recruiter Through Official Channels
Treat every unsolicited offer as unverified until proven otherwise. Ask for an email from the recruiter's corporate domain and a calendar invite from the same domain. If you're unsure, call the company's main line and ask to confirm the contact.

---

## 💰 8. Never Deposit Checks and Send Money Back
Never bank on a "cleared" check. No honest potential employer will ever send you a check to deposit and then tell you to send on part of the money or buy gift cards with it — that's a fake check scam.

---

## 📋 9. Be Skeptical of Vague Job Descriptions
Fake job postings often have vague requirements. Be cautious of opportunities that only ask for simple criteria, like being of legal age or knowing how to type, as these broad qualifications may indicate that the job is not genuine.

---

## 🌐 10. Stick to Reputable Job Platforms & Save Evidence
Always verify the employer through independent searches and visit the company's official website to confirm that the job is listed there. Stick to reputable job search websites and professional networks — they are less likely to have job scams, but they can still happen. Save evidence — screenshots, URLs, and message histories help platforms and companies take action.

---

## 🚨 What to Do If You've Been Scammed
If you sent money, personal information, or gave computer access to a scammer, visit the **Federal Trade Commission (FTC)** at ftc.gov to report it.

Stay cautious and trust your instincts — if something feels off, it probably is. Take a step back and consult someone you trust. The greater the sense of urgency and the greater the opportunity, the more likely it is a scam.
